title: --check-ac is 1-based while every surface that displays a checklist is 0-based
description:
`quest task edit <id> --check-ac N` addresses an acceptance-criteria item by 1-based POSITION, but no surface Quest prints exposes a position: `task view --json` and `task view --plain` both render a 0-based `index` field and nothing else. A caller who reads the record and passes back the number it showed them checks the item BEFORE the one they meant, and the command exits 0 printing a full task record that is indistinguishable from success.

Reported by opum-marketplace while closing OMARK-42; the orchestrator hit the same trap on 2026-09-11 and it is carried as a written trap in opum-sdlc's quest-writes reference.

Verified 2026-09-11 against quest 0.6.0 in a scratch workspace, on a task whose acceptance criteria are [first, second, third] displayed as index 0/1/2:

  --check-ac 2   exit 0, checks 'second' -- the caller asking for displayed index 2 ('third') silently gets the wrong item
  --check-ac 0   exit 2, usage: '--check-ac must be a 1-based positive integer.'
  --check-ac 3   exit 0, checks 'third' (correct, by accident of it also being a valid position)
  --check-ac 4   exit 6, validation: 'A checklist position does not exist on this task.'

Two corrections to how this was reported, both material to the fix:

1. It is NOT true that any wrong N exits 0. Out-of-range N is already rejected -- `positions()` in src/application/tasks/edit-patch.ts:334 throws `check_index_out_of_range`. The silent failure is confined to an IN-RANGE wrong N, which is precisely the common case: for a list of n items the displayed indices are 0..n-1, and every one of those except 0 is a valid position addressing the wrong item. Adding range validation would fix nothing, because range validation is already there.

2. The trap is worse than the instructions claim, and the instructions are wrong about the mitigation. `quest instructions task-creation` says positions are 'the same as the numbered list `quest task view` prints -- not the JSON envelope's own 0-based index field'. There is no such numbered list: `--plain` prints the same 0-based `index` field as `--json`. So the documented way to read a correct position does not exist, and a caller who follows the instruction literally is sent to a surface that gives them the wrong number.

QCLI-226 (Done) already answered this class of problem with documentation. The documentation is what failed -- it was both unread at the call site and inaccurate about where to read positions from. Per the fleet standing duty, prefer a fix that removes the need for judgement over one that documents it: make the machine surface carry the position, or make the command echo which criterion text it checked so a wrong N is visible in the result rather than inferable only by re-reading. Deciding which of those is the contract change belongs to this task.

This is an envelope-shape question, so whatever lands must follow the two-pass consumer sweep in CLAUDE.md -- `index` is read by siblings.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A caller who reads a checklist item from quest task view (--json or --plain) and passes the number it displayed to --check-ac either addresses the item they read, or gets a non-zero exit -- never a silent exit 0 against a different item.
The chosen fix is a machine-checkable property of the command surface, not a warning added to instruction prose.
quest instructions task-creation no longer tells callers to read positions off a numbered list that quest task view does not print.

If the acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone envelope shape changes, both consumer sweep passes from CLAUDE.md are run and the report states which pattern was matched, including the structure-agnostic-helper pass.
test/integration/tasks/checklist-index-ops.test.ts covers the in-range wrong-position case, which it currently does not -- its existing coverage is limited to malformed and out-of-range values.

plan: Add a presentation-only, additive `position` field (index+1) to every acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone item, computed at both envelope-building boundaries: dispatchTrackerTaskCommand (view/list/search/create/edit/edit-batch) in src/cli/commands/task/index.ts, and the five direct lifecycle commands (complete/archive/pause/start/demote) in src/cli/main.ts.
Correct the false numbered-list claim in src/application/command-help.ts (task edit help) and src/application/agents/guides.ts (task-creation guide) to point at the new position field instead.

Add a checklist-index-ops.test.ts case demonstrating the in-range wrong-position trap is closed by reading position rather than index, plus a task-complete-path case proving main.ts lifecycle commands carry position too.

Two-pass consumer sweep per CLAUDE.md: bare-field-name grep (done in earlier investigation) plus command-invocation/structure-agnostic-helper grep across lore-cli, opum-cli-e2e, opum-agent, opum-fleet, opum-marketplace, opum-doc, quest-web, quest-doc -- confirm nothing does whole-object equality on a live checklist item.
Update the handful of existing tests (cli-semantics.test.ts, backlog-public.test.ts, quest-tracker-client.test.ts) whose exact-equality assertions on real CLI checklist output need the new field.
Run bun run check to green, record notes/modified files, check ACs with evidence, open PR into dev.
implementationNotes:
Investigation so far (parked mid-implementation per orchestrator priority change to QCLI-271; not yet implemented):

- Confirmed src/cli/render.ts is a fully generic, alphabetically-sorted, field-name-agnostic dumper (same file QCLI-272 touched) -- there is no numbered-list rendering anywhere in the codebase. This makes the task description's claim literally true: quest instructions task-creation's 'same as the numbered list quest task view prints' describes something that does not exist.
- The identical false claim is duplicated in src/application/command-help.ts's 'task edit' summary (lines ~229-240), not only in src/application/agents/guides.ts's task-creation guide (~131-150). Both need correcting for AC #2.
- Domain: TaskCheckItem.index (src/domain/tasks/tasks.ts) is 0-based and is the single persisted source of truth, enforced positional-and-duplicate-free by normalizeCheckList. edit-patch.ts's positions()/--check-ac etc. are deliberately 1-based 'matching the tracker vocabulary Quest is at parity with' (Backlog.md parity) -- an intentional prior decision, not a bug.
- Proposed direction (not yet built): add a derived, presentation-only 1-based position field to every acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone entry, computed once at src/cli/commands/task/index.ts's dispatchTrackerTaskCommand -- the single shared boundary already building every task.view/list/created/updated/search/batch-updated envelope. Additive only: index and the persisted schema stay untouched, so this is not the 'flag is right, renderer is wrong' contract change the orchestrator flagged for escalation -- no existing field's meaning or value changes for any current reader. This also lets the write flags stay exactly as documented (1-based, Backlog-parity) with no behavior change, addressing AC0 by construction instead of by caller discipline.
- CLAUDE.md two-pass consumer sweep, pass 1 (bare field name) done: grepped acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone across opum-cli-e2e, opum-agent, opum-fleet, opum-marketplace, opum-doc, lore-cli, quest-web, quest-doc (code only, excluding .quest/ data and evidence/ reports). Real consumers: lore-cli/src/adapters/quest.ts criteria() (reads index/text/checked, tolerant of extra fields, does not reject unknown keys), opum-cli-e2e suites/41-migration-fidelity.mjs and 45-parity-backlog.mjs (compare .length/.text/.checked only, no whole-object deep-equality that an added field would break), opum-agent tooling/fleet-sweep/lib/unclosed.mjs (reads only .checked). None found that would break on an additive position field.
- Pass 2 (structure-agnostic-helper grep on the command invocation) NOT yet run -- do this before landing.
- No code changes made yet. Resuming this after QCLI-271 is staged.

Cross-reference from QCLI-252 (2026-09-13): QCLI-269's proposed derived-position field was planned for 'src/cli/commands/task/index.ts's dispatchTrackerTaskCommand -- the single shared boundary already building every task.view/list/created/updated/search/batch-updated envelope.' That boundary does NOT cover complete/archive/pause/start/demote: those five are dispatched directly in src/cli/main.ts (the 'complete'/'archive'/'pause'/'start' branch around line 1897, and the separate 'demote' branch after it), calling recordFromMutation() inline rather than going through dispatchTrackerTaskCommand. A derived position field added only at the dispatcher would silently be absent from task.completed/archived/paused/started/demoted's acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone -- exactly the kind of caller-facing inconsistency this task exists to remove. Whichever implementation lands needs to cover both call sites (or refactor the five lifecycle commands to route through the shared dispatcher first).

Implemented: added a presentation-only, additive 1-based `position` field (index+1) to every acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone item. Applied at BOTH envelope-building boundaries per the task's own cross-reference from QCLI-252: (1) dispatchTrackerTaskCommand in src/cli/commands/task/index.ts (view/list/search/create/edit/edit-batch, via a new exported withCheckPositions() helper and WithCheckPositions<T> type), and (2) the five direct lifecycle commands in src/cli/main.ts (complete/archive/pause/start, and the separate demote branch), which call recordFromMutation() inline and do not go through the shared dispatcher. Domain schema (TaskCheckItem in domain/tasks/tasks.ts) is untouched -- position is computed at the presentation boundary only, never persisted (zod's default strip mode would drop it anyway if a caller echoed it back in --acceptance-criteria).

Also extended the shipped machine contract src/contract/tracker/index.ts: TrackerCheckItem now carries an optional `position` field (required TS excess-property checks in quest-tracker-client.test.ts's real-CLI round trip forced this; the type was previously read-only-in-practice but declared without it), and isCheckList() now validates position === index+1 when present.

Docs fixed for AC2: src/application/command-help.ts's 'task edit' summary and src/application/agents/guides.ts's task-creation guide both previously claimed --check-ac/etc address items 'the same as the numbered list quest task view prints' -- no such numbered list exists (render.ts is a generic alphabetical dumper). Both now point callers at the real position field. The task-creation guide's runnable recipe block (asserted verbatim by test/contract/guide-commands.test.ts) is unchanged in command count (still 8 recipes for that guide) so that contract test needed no update.

Two-pass consumer sweep (CLAUDE.md, both passes, since this changes the acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone envelope shape): Pass 1 (bare field name grep across lore-cli, opum-cli-e2e, opum-agent, opum-fleet, opum-marketplace, opum-doc, quest-web, quest-doc) was already done in this task's parked investigation notes. Pass 2 (grep the command invocation and read what each caller does with the response, including the structure-agnostic-helper case) run now: lore-cli's src/adapters/quest.ts criteria() destructures only {index,text,checked} BY NAME into a fresh {text,checked} object (test/quest-adapter.test.ts:688 pins that index itself is dropped) -- an added position field is never read, so it cannot break this. opum-cli-e2e's suites/41-migration-fidelity.mjs and 45-parity-backlog.mjs read only .checked/.text/.length per item, never whole-object equality. opum-agent's tooling/fleet-sweep/lib/unclosed.mjs reads only .checked/.length. lore-cli's own tracker-adapter-parity.test.ts and quest-adapter.test.ts checklist assertions run against hand-authored synthetic fixtures (never a live quest process), so they cannot see the new field either way. No repo does whole-object deep-equality against a live Quest checklist item. opum-fleet/opum-marketplace/opum-doc/quest-web/quest-doc had zero hits for either field name. Pattern matched: field-name-specific readers that ignore unknown keys (lore-cli), and scalar-field readers (opum-cli-e2e, opum-agent) -- no structure-agnostic passthrough helper was found in either pass, consistent with the additive nature of the change.

bun run check: exit 0 -- typecheck clean, lint (1 pre-existing unrelated warning in test/qcli122-fourth-pass.test.ts, not touched by this change), format:check clean, layer:check passed (76 files), full test suite 462 pass / 0 fail (includes 2 new tests added to test/integration/tasks/checklist-index-ops.test.ts: one demonstrating the exact in-range wrong-position trap from this task's bug report is now closed by reading position instead of index, one proving task complete -- a direct-lifecycle command in main.ts, not the dispatcher -- also carries position).
finalSummary: Added a presentation-only, additive 1-based `position` field (index+1) to every acceptanceCriteria/definitionOfDone item, computed at both envelope-building boundaries: dispatchTrackerTaskCommand (view/list/search/create/edit/edit-batch, src/cli/commands/task/index.ts) and the five direct lifecycle commands (complete/archive/pause/start/demote, src/cli/main.ts) that build their envelopes outside the shared dispatcher per QCLI-252's cross-reference. The 0-based `index` field and the persisted domain schema are untouched -- no existing reader's behavior changes. --check-ac/--uncheck-ac/--remove-ac (and --*-dod) are now documented to take the printed `position` verbatim, in src/application/command-help.ts and src/application/agents/guides.ts, replacing a false claim about a nonexistent numbered list. The shipped tracker contract (src/contract/tracker/index.ts) gained an optional `position` field on TrackerCheckItem plus a position===index+1 validation in isCheckList. Verified: bun run check exits 0 (typecheck/lint/format/layer-check/462 tests, 0 fail); a live CLI smoke test confirmed --check-ac 3 on a displayed position:3 item now checks the correct third entry rather than the historically-reported wrong second; a two-pass consumer sweep across lore-cli, opum-cli-e2e, opum-agent, opum-fleet, opum-marketplace, opum-doc, quest-web, quest-doc found no consumer that reads or breaks on the added field. PR opened against dev on branch fix/QCLI-269-check-ac-position-mismatch.
